The error message indicates that there are duplicate index values in the concatenated DataFrame. The `verify_integrity` option is used to check for duplicate index values and raise a ValueError if they exist.

However, based on the provided code, it seems that this is not the cause of the issue. 

The real issue here is likely due to the fact that the `df3` DataFrame has overlapping columns with `df1`, but it also has an additional column 'animal'. When concatenating these DataFrames along axis=0 (default), pandas will include all columns from both DataFrames, even if they are not present in every row. This can lead to unexpected behavior and errors.

To fix this issue, you can use the `concat` function with the `join` parameter set to `'inner'`. This will return only the columns that exist in both DataFrames:

```python
pd.concat([df1, df3], join="inner")
```

Alternatively, if you want to keep all columns from both DataFrames, you can use the `concat` function with the `axis` parameter set to 1 (horizontal concatenation), and then reset the index of the resulting DataFrame:

```python
pd.concat([df1, df3], axis=1).reset_index(drop=True)
```

This will ensure that the resulting DataFrame has a consistent index.
